Hi Sarah / Jordan — quick technical scheduling note from our side.

We can do Mar 9 at 10:00 AM AEDT, but because US DST starts on Sun Mar 8, folks on the US East Coast may see the event shift by an hour in their calendars depending on when the invite was created. Practically that can cause a 1-hour mismatch for any US attendees who keep local time. The safe approaches are:

1) Anchor the invite in UTC (I recommend this) and indicate the UTC time in the subject and body e.g., "Mar 9, 23:00 UTC" — that way clients with different DST rules see the correct mapping.
2) Move the meeting to Mar 10 (post-DST change) to avoid anyone juggling the cutover day.

If Mark is in Dublin (UTC+0) and Sarah is in AEDT (UTC+11), Option A maps to 23:00 UTC on Mar 8 (which is late for Dublin but acceptable). If we do Mar 10 14:00 UTC that converts to:
• Mar 11 01:00 AEDT (Sydney) — probably too late for Sarah
• Mar 10 14:00 UTC is Mar 10 10:00 CET for Dublin — closer to business hours.

Given the tradeoffs, I suggest: keep the meeting in business hours for Aurelia (you asked for Mar 9 morning AEDT). If that’s preferred, Jordan — please send a UTC-anchored invite and include a short note: "Note: US DST begins 2026-03-08; time listed in UTC to avoid calendar shifts." I’ll be on the call.

Also — if Mark prefers a different slot (earlier for Dublin), happy to offer two 30-min blocks so we can avoid stretching late for Sydney.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
